owner: REASONING COACH (Claude Desktop d82c3a44), policy only
consumer: AI HARNESS 8e75e3: the selector lives in CEE and writes TS predicates over the named signals below. PANEL renders. No second, UI-side guidance system (DL 5930647566).
contract: acceptance-cases.json is the behaviour contract. The harness imports it into its vitest suite and runs its real selector against it. check-policy.mjs only lints this file's shape.
principles: Coach the user's reasoning, not the graph. Every row leads with a decision question in the user's words; the model action comes second.
Trigger only on typed canonical state (the signals below). Never on text heuristics over chat, never on regex.
A signal that is pending or absent means SILENCE, never a fallback guess.
One intervention at a time. A decision point always outranks a method.
A pressed, dismissed or completed intervention returns only when its state_key changes, or the user asks for it.
Never diagnose the user. Describe the pattern, say why it matters, offer a test.
Never state a science number that is on the never_coach list. Never claim nothing would change the answer.

user.explicit_request.meaning: The user invoked this method by name (menu item, pill, or typed chip id). Bypasses cooldown; still records 'pressed'.

selection.run_result_rule: Request 1 carries only the typed result and the 'Explain this result' chip (agent-explain-run:<run_key>). No coaching row is offered on request 1.
selection.explain_this_result: A continuation of the Run, not a coaching intervention. It never counts against the budget below.
selection.suppression: If open.decision_point is true, offer NO coaching row and no RC-COACH-EDITS pill. The decision comes first.

budget.slot_1: The single highest-priority eligible row among RC-WIDEN, RC-WHAT-CHANGES, RC-STRENGTHEN-ITEM, RC-PREMORTEM.
budget.slot_2: RC-COACH-EDITS, only when eligible. It is user-initiated, so it may sit beside slot 1.

tie_break: Same priority and the SAME item (e.g. RC-WHAT-CHANGES and RC-STRENGTHEN-ITEM both name factor X): offer RC-WHAT-CHANGES only. Reasoning framing wins over the model action.
Otherwise by row order: RC-WIDEN, RC-WHAT-CHANGES, RC-STRENGTHEN-ITEM, RC-PREMORTEM.
selection.method_turn_rule: On a 'method' turn, offer no other method. Offer only that method's own follow-up actions.
selection.cooldown_default: A row (or item) with guidance status pressed, dismissed or completed is not offered while its current state_key_hash equals the recorded one. user.explicit_request bypasses this.
selection.state_key_persistence: Persist state_key as a SHA-256 hex prefix (12 chars) of the canonical JSON of its fields. Never persist raw values (coaching_state is content-free).
selection.cold_reload: Guidance must round-trip through coaching_state: a pressed or dismissed row stays hidden after a cold reload with an unchanged state_key (#2388 two-load lesson).
selection.cooldown_scope: Variant rows (RC-WIDEN): pick the first variant that holds, THEN apply cooldown to that pick; a row in cooldown does NOT fall through to its later variants (case A-WIDEN-SAME-KEY-HIDDEN: W1 dismissed, W2 also holds, RC-WIDEN stays hidden). Item rows (RC-STRENGTHEN-ITEM): cooldown is per item, so a cooled item falls through to the next candidate in pick order, and across variants (S1, then S2, S3L, S3V).

rows.name: Widen the options

variants.when: run.kind == complete_current AND run.withheld_reason in [no_option_meets_limit, every_option_likely_breaks_limit]

trigger_predicate.pick: The first variant that holds, in the order listed.

silent_when: open.decision_point
turn.request == run_result
guidance[RC-WIDEN] is pressed, dismissed or completed with an unchanged state_key
the only reason would be to reach a count; never add items for their own sake
rows.priority: per variant (W1, W2 = P1; W3-W6 = P3; W7 = P5)

reasoning_question.W1: None of these looks likely to stay within your limit. Is there another way to get there?
reasoning_question.W2: Is it really just {option_label} or carry on as now? What other routes are there?
reasoning_question.W3: These options all pull the same lever. Is there a different way to reach the goal?
reasoning_question.W4: Would carrying on as now be a real option worth comparing against?
reasoning_question.W5: These options come out about the same. Is there a hybrid that takes the best of each?
reasoning_question.W6: What else could stop this working?

short_copy.W1: Every option looks likely to break your limit. Worth finding another route?
short_copy.W2: Only one real option on the table. Decisions go better with alternatives.
short_copy.W3: These options all work through the same lever. A different mechanism?
short_copy.W4: Comparing against 'carry on as now' shows what each change really adds.
short_copy.W5: The options come out close. A hybrid might beat both.
short_copy.W6: Only one risk is on the map. What else could go wrong?
short_copy.W7: Few drivers are mapped for {goal_label}. What else moves it?

why_now.W1: The analysis checked your limit and no option clears it.
why_now.W2: There is one option besides carrying on as now.
why_now.W3: Most of the options change the same factors.
why_now.W4: There is no 'carry on as now' option to compare with.
why_now.W5: The analysis could not separate the options.
why_now.W6: The model has at most one risk.
why_now.W7: Two or fewer factors lead to the goal.

primary_action.behaviour: Olumi proposes up to 3 materially distinct items, each grounded in the brief or the model, starting with any Olumi-proposed option already left out of the comparison. They are shown as decision-point buttons ('Add' per item, plus 'Something else'). Nothing is added until the user chooses.

rows.progressive_detail: Why: one line on the variant's why_now, with its source (Grammar §3 coaching pattern). Detail on click: the science basis in one sentence.

bias_cue.narrow_framing: These options all work through the same lever, which can hide better routes.
bias_cue.status_quo: Without a 'carry on as now' option it is hard to see what each change really adds.

state_key.note: W2-W4 and W7 keys exclude withheld_reason, so a new limit verdict alone does not bring the row back. Options added through this method change the key; the row returns only while a variant still holds.

rows.reentry_rule: Returns only when the option set (or risk set for W6) or withheld_reason changes AND a variant still holds.
rows.completion_rule: Completed when the user adds at least one proposed item, or chooses 'Something else' / says none apply.
rows.human_control_rule: Never adds an option, risk or factor without the user's choice. Each accepted item lands as ONE change card (before, after, Apply, Edit, Undo).

science_basis.summary: Decisions framed with a single alternative ('whether or not') fail more often than ones with real alternatives; generating options before evaluating is a core decision-quality step.

rows.name: What would change the decision?
silent_when: open.decision_point
turn.request == run_result
run.decision_sensitivity.status in [none_measurable, not_measured]
run.kind != complete_current (stale, withheld or no run)
run.leader_licensed != true
guidance[RC-WHAT-CHANGES] pressed, dismissed or completed with an unchanged state_key

reasoning_question.range_olumi_assumed: Do you know {factor_label} more precisely? Within Olumi's assumed range it could change which option leads.
reasoning_question.range_yours_or_unknown: Would {leader_label} still be the best choice if {factor_label} turned out different?

rows.why_now: The analysis found that the answer is sensitive to {factor_label}.
rows.progressive_detail: Click reveals: which figure it is, whose figure it is (yours / Olumi's estimate), and one line on what the analysis varied. No numbers from never_coach.
rows.reentry_rule: Returns after a new Run whose most sensitive factor differs, or after that factor's value or authorship changed.
rows.completion_rule: Completed when the user gives an estimate for the factor, or the method turn answers (discussed).
rows.human_control_rule: Never changes the value. An estimate the user gives goes through the normal inline edit and is recorded as theirs.
never_say: a win probability or 'chance it wins'
EVPI, EVPPI, elasticity, sensitivity score, 'strongest driver'
'No single assumption measurably changes which option leads' or any claim that nothing would change the answer (factor_evppi is structurally flat in additive lever models, P3C A2)
'assumption' when only factor values were varied; say 'this figure'

science_basis.summary: Expected value of partial perfect information ranks which uncertain input could change the choice. Attention goes to the input that matters to the decision, not the one with the biggest structural weight.

rows.note: Expect this row to fire rarely today: factor_evppi is structurally flat in additive lever models (P3C A2), and every served run read on 1 Oct had EVPPI empty or below resolution and every flip_thresholds row no_flip_in_range. Silence is the correct output there. It fires once identity kinds (product, stock-flow) make a factor interact with a lever.

refs: Spetzler & Staël von Holstein (1975) probability encoding

rows.name: Pre-mortem

trigger_predicate.explicit_request: On user.explicit_request with a goal and at least one option, run it at any stage. With no current Run, use the qualitative protocol: no invented winner, probability or figure (SCI-09).

forbidden_without: a plan to stress: a licensed leader, or a single option with a risk on the map, or an explicit request

turn.request == run_result

reasoning_question.undated: Imagine {plan_label} has gone badly. What most likely went wrong?

primary_action.behaviour: Olumi writes 2-3 plausible failure stories. Each one must name at least one model item: a risk node, an Olumi-estimated link on the plan's path, or a limit at risk. For each: one warning sign to watch and one mitigation. Presented as stories, never as predictions.

secondary_actions.label: Add this as a risk
secondary_actions.note: A change card; nothing is added without Apply.

fields: leader option id if licensed else the single option id

science_basis.summary: Prospective hindsight (imagining the failure has already happened) surfaces more and more specific reasons for failure than asking what might go wrong.
refs: Klein (2007) Performing a project premortem, HBR

waiting_library.rule: Deterministic, no LLM call, no added latency. Rotate within the current phase only. Never claim progress that has not happened. Result-first always wins: drop the line the moment the result is ready. Each line is 90 characters or fewer.

phase_of.reading_brief: the brief has been sent and drafting has not produced structure yet

reading_brief: Good decisions start with the real question, not the first one that comes to mind.
Decisions with real alternatives tend to go better than 'whether or not' choices.
A goal written as a number makes it easier to tell which option gets there.
structuring: Separating what you control from what you can't makes trade-offs easier to see.
A cause-and-effect map shows which assumptions your choice actually rests on.
Each figure is marked as yours or Olumi's estimate, so you can see what to check.
running_analysis: The analysis tries many combinations of the uncertain values in your model.
Results show what follows from the model's assumptions, not a forecast.
Often one or two figures decide the choice. Those are the ones worth checking.
preparing_explanation: Olumi only puts an option forward when the analysis supports it.
A result is only as strong as the figures behind it. Look for which are yours.
Where a figure is Olumi's estimate, your own number can sharpen the answer.

structuring: Howard (1988) decision analysis: decisions vs uncertainties
running_analysis: SCI-04: simulation frequency is not real-world probability

waiting_library.panel_swap: PANEL: replace the METHOD_CATALOGUE-derived WAITING_COACHING_LINES in src/canvas/conversation/zones/ThinkingDots.tsx with lines[phase] for the current phase.
waiting_library.honesty: Every line passes DGAI's narration-honesty rules (src/canvas/components/__tests__/narrationHonesty.invariant.spec.ts @ 637b36da): the base rules (no pipeline-stage verbs, no judging the brief, no typical-duration claims, no completion-proximity, no percentages or step counts) and the frame-licence rules (no recommendation, leader, probability, freshness or completion words). check-policy.mjs runs the same patterns.

copy_rules.label_fill: Fill {placeholders} from typed labels only; truncate a label to 40 characters with an ellipsis.
copy_rules.voice: British English, sentence case, no em dashes, no all caps, no error codes (DS v5 §29).
copy_rules.response_shape: One-line insight, then at most 3 bullets, then one action or question; details collapsed (Grammar §3).
copy_rules.label_case: Option labels ({option_label}, {plan_label}, {leader_label}) are quoted in single curly quotes and keep their case: 'Imagine ‘Switch to GCP’ has failed.' Other mid-sentence labels lower-case their first letter unless the first word is an acronym or proper noun (second letter upper-case, e.g. 'GCP', 'AI'). A label that opens the sentence keeps its capital.

user_language.risk: Something that might happen and would hurt the goal (an event or exposure). Example: 'a key engineer leaves'.
user_language.negative_factor: A quantity where more of it hurts the goal. Example: 'monthly cloud spend'.
user_language.adverse_outcome: The bad result itself. Example: 'missing the funding target'.
user_language.constraint: A limit you will not cross. Example: 'churn must stay under 3%'.
user_language.uncertainty: How sure we are about a figure or a link.
user_language.status: Draft user-language mapping for display and coaching only. No node-type or schema change. MG (F1) to confirm the model semantics.

method_turns.purpose: What a method must produce when pressed. Every post_check is a DETERMINISTIC text rule with an id (Ticket 1 implements all of them in checkMethodTurn). Rules that need structured output are listed under structured_checks; they are AI HARNESS's (method-turn output format) and are NOT part of the text checker. If a text check fails, send the deterministic fallback instead.

shared.shape: One-line insight, then the method's body, then ONE action (Grammar §3). Details collapsed.
shared.grounding: Only the typed inputs listed per method plus the user's own words. Every specific claim names a supplied item by its label or ref (O1, F2, R1).
never: a probability, percentage or win share unless the user stated it
a leading option when run.leader_licensed is false
'the model was saved', implementation detail, internal ids
EVPI, elasticity, sensitivity score, placeholder, edge, node

parsing.numbered_items: items start on a new line with /^\s*[1-9]\.\s/ ; an item runs until the next numbered line or the end
parsing.bullet_items: items start on a new line with /^\s*-\s/ ; the item NAME is the text before the first ':' on that line
parsing.normalise: lower-case, curly quotes to straight, strip punctuation and collapse whitespace
parsing.label_match: case-insensitive substring match of a supplied label after normalise, or a supplied ref (O1, F2, R1) as a whole word
parsing.number_tokens: /(?<![A-Za-z])[£$€]?\d[\d,]*(\.\d+)?\s*(%|k|m|bn)?/i, ignoring list markers at the start of a line; a token is 'supplied' if its digits appear in the inputs, the brief or the user's messages

inputs: plan: option label + ref (leader if licensed, else the single user option)
goal label, target and horizon if set
risk nodes on the plan's path: label + ref
links on the plan's path with link_sizing placeholder or olumi_estimate: from/to labels
limits: label + verdict class (met | likely broken | not checked)
figures the user stated (label + value)
RC-PREMORTEM.body: 2-3 failure stories told in the past tense ('It is a year later and ‘Switch to GCP’ went badly because…'). Each story: one or two sentences, names at least one supplied item, then 'Watch for:' one early warning sign and 'Mitigate:' one action.
RC-PREMORTEM.action: 'Add this as a risk' (a change card for one story's risk, nothing added without Apply) or 'Talk it through'.

post_checks.rule: 2 <= numbered_items <= 3
every numbered item label_matches >= 1 supplied label or ref
every numbered item contains 'Watch for:' and 'Mitigate:'
no '%' and no /\b(likely|likelihood|chance|probability|probable|odds)\b/i anywhere
no /\b(will|is going to|are going to) fail\b/i
no current option label other than the plan's label_matches

RC-PREMORTEM.fallback: Deterministic, no LLM: 'Imagine ‘{plan}’ has gone badly. Start with {first risk or Olumi-estimated link}: how would you notice it early, and what would you do?' plus the 'Talk it through' action.
RC-PREMORTEM.science: Prospective hindsight (Mitchell, Russo & Pennington 1989; Klein 2007; DSK-P-001).
RC-PREMORTEM.format: Insight line, then 2-3 stories as a numbered list; each story contains 'Watch for:' and 'Mitigate:'.

inputs: goal label and target
current user options: label + ref + the factors each one changes
Olumi-proposed options left out of the comparison: label + ref
limits: label + verdict class
variant (W1-W7) and target (options | risks | factors)
the brief, verbatim
RC-WIDEN.body: Up to 3 items that work through a materially DIFFERENT mechanism from the current ones (options), or name a different way the plan could fail (risks), or a different driver of the goal (factors). Each item: a name of 6 words or fewer, then one line saying what it changes and why it might do better. Start with any Olumi-proposed option already left out of the comparison.
RC-WIDEN.action: Decision-point buttons: 'Add' per item, then 'Something else' (choose_1_of_3). Each Add lands as ONE change card.

post_checks.rule: 1 <= bullet_items <= 3
no bullet NAME equals (after normalise) a CURRENT user option, risk or factor label; supplied left-out Olumi option labels are exempt
every number_token in the reply is supplied
variant W1 only: no bullet matches /\b(meets?|clears?|stays? (within|under)|within)\b[^.]{0,40}\blimit\b/i

RC-WIDEN.fallback: Deterministic: list the Olumi-proposed options left out (if any) as Add buttons; else 'What other way could you reach {goal}? For example, a different lever, a smaller first step, or a mix of these options.' with 'Talk it through'.
RC-WIDEN.science: Generating alternatives before evaluating; 'whether or not' framing fails more often (Nutt 1999; Keeney 1992; DSK-P-004, DSK-B-007).
RC-WIDEN.format: Insight line, then 1-3 items as bullets '- {name}: {one line on what it changes}'.

structured_checks.owner: AI HARNESS (method-turn output format); NOT in Ticket 1's text checker
structured_checks.why: A materially different option usually works through a lever that is not in the model yet, so free text cannot be checked against model factors.
structured_checks.requires: the method turn returns items as {name, mechanism_kind: new_lever | hybrid | left_out_option | existing_factor, refs[]}

checks.rule: mechanism_kind hybrid: refs include >= 2 current option refs
mechanism_kind existing_factor: the factor ref is not in the current options' shared lever set
mechanism_kind left_out_option: name equals a supplied left-out option label
mechanism_kind new_lever: name and lever do not normalise-equal any shared-lever factor label

inputs: decision_sensitivity.most_sensitive: factor label + ref, current value + unit, whose figure (yours | Olumi's estimate), range source
leader label (licensed only)
other compared options: labels
RC-WHAT-CHANGES.body: One line on what the analysis varied ('Olumi varied {factor} within the range it assumed'). Then up to 3 bullets on what would have to be true about {factor} for a different option to come out ahead, said qualitatively. Then the question asking for the user's estimate.
RC-WHAT-CHANGES.action: 'Give your estimate' (edit_inline on the factor) when the range is Olumi's; else 'Talk it through'.

post_checks.rule: label_matches the supplied factor label
every number_token is the factor's current value or a user figure
no /nothing would change|no single (assumption|factor)/i
no /\b(EVPI|EVPPI|sensitivity score|elasticity)\b/i and no '%'

RC-WHAT-CHANGES.fallback: Deterministic: the row's reasoning_question with the 'Give your estimate' action.
RC-WHAT-CHANGES.science: Value of information: attention goes to the input that can change the choice (Howard 1966).
RC-WHAT-CHANGES.format: Insight line naming what was varied, up to 3 bullets on what would have to be true, then the question.

inputs: the item: link (from/to labels) or factor (label, current value + unit)
whose figure (link_sizing / value_authorship)
options whose goal figures depend on it
RC-STRENGTHEN-ITEM.body: Up to 3 bullets: what the figure means in plain words; one cheap way to pin it down (a number the user may already have, a quick test, someone to ask); what the user's own estimate would change for the comparison.
RC-STRENGTHEN-ITEM.action: 'Give your estimate' (edit_inline), with 'Use Olumi's estimate' (confirm) as the secondary.

post_checks.rule: label_matches the item's label (both labels for a link)
no /\b(placeholder|edge|node|default strength)\b/i
every number_token is the item's current value or a user figure

RC-STRENGTHEN-ITEM.fallback: Deterministic: the row's reasoning_question with the inline edit.
RC-STRENGTHEN-ITEM.format: Up to 3 bullets: what the figure means, one cheap way to pin it down, what the user's estimate would change.

inputs: uncoached goal-path edits: label, field, before, after
options whose path the edited item sits on
run.kind (current | stale)
RC-COACH-EDITS.body: One-line insight. Then at most 3 bullets: (1) what changed, before and after; (2) the assumption or trade-off it touches; (3) which conclusion may now change. Last line, only if run.kind is complete_stale: 'The analysis is out of date.' and offer a rerun.
RC-COACH-EDITS.action: 'Rerun' only when stale and the model may run; else none (coaching only).

post_checks.rule: label_matches every edited item's label (up to 3)
/out of date/i present if and only if run.kind == complete_stale
no /\b(the result (has )?changed|now leads|is now ahead|the answer is now)\b/i

RC-COACH-EDITS.fallback: Deterministic: 'You changed {edit list}. That changes {assumption}. ' + the stale line when stale.
RC-COACH-EDITS.science: Timely feedback on one's own change (Kahneman & Klein 2009); consider the implications (DSK-P-003).
RC-COACH-EDITS.format: Insight line, then up to 3 bullets (what changed, the assumption it touches, what may change), then the stale line only if stale.

ui_trigger_map.rule: ONE guidance mechanism (DL 5930647566): the Reasoning tab renders the CEE selector's slot-1 row as its 'next reasoning step' and keeps METHOD_CATALOGUE as the always-available on-demand menu. UI-side triggers that pick methods are retired as the selector serves; until then they may stay, but none may contradict a row's silence rule.

strengthen:robustness -> pre_mortem.reads: robustness.level low|very_low and leader not withheld
strengthen:robustness -> pre_mortem.why: Robustness is caveat-only (P3C: 'no option comes top in most of Olumi's simulations over estimated links'); a fragile result is not execution risk. RC-PREMORTEM fires on a licensed leader.

strengthen:broaden / LOW_OPTION_COUNT ->.reads: bias finding types in NARROW_TYPES (draft-pipeline label heuristics or decision-review prose); producer LOW_OPTION_COUNT
strengthen:broaden / LOW_OPTION_COUNT ->.why: Same move, but RC-WIDEN keys on typed option counts and detectSameLeverOptions, not keywords.

strengthen:flip -> consider_opposite.reads: top producer fragile_edges row by switch_probability, gated on a licensed leader and attestsNoFactorFlip
strengthen:flip -> consider_opposite.why: It shows switch_probability as 'NN% chance'. At ISL staging 04836e20 (robustness_analyzer_v2.py:10990-11040, CODE-READ) that is the share of weak-link draws an alternative wins, with no base rate subtracted; when the leader still wins those draws it reports the runner-up's share. It describes the runner-up, not the link's effect (P3C never-coach).

COGNITIVE_BIAS -> review_bias; anchoring.why: Untyped prose. Bias lines come only from RC-WIDEN bias_cue (typed); the menu item stays on demand.
